video.title: Watch Me Clone a $200K/Month Business in 5 Minutes

summary: Chris Koerner walks through GoHighLevel's public SaaSpreneur awards page, which lists white-label resellers by customer tier (gold 100+, platinum 500+, diamond 1,000+). He estimates revenue by multiplying public pricing by tier customer counts, then reverse-engineers businesses selling to local service niches: event rentals (Event Hawk), med spas, gyms (PushPress) and dental (Dental Implant Machine). His toolkit is the pricing page, Wayback Machine, Meta Ads Library, BuiltWith and LinkedIn. He ends with a live demo of a missed-call-text-back setup for roofers in GoHighLevel. The key takeaway is to pick a boring local niche, copy proven ads and offers, and resell white-labelled software, but all figures are his napkin estimates and he earns affiliate commission from GoHighLevel.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office, Dallas-based, GoHighLevel affiliate and user.

ideas.name: White-label GoHighLevel SaaS reseller for a local-service niche
ideas.one_liner: Rebrand GoHighLevel as your own niche marketing/CRM software and resell it to local businesses at $97+/month per customer.
ideas.business_model: Monthly subscription (reselled white-label software), often bundled with done-for-you marketing services.
ideas.customer: Local service businesses (event rentals, med spas, gyms, dentists, roofers, pest control).
ideas.problem: Local businesses miss leads and bookings and lack marketing/CRM systems.
ideas.offer: Own-branded all-in-one marketing, booking, phone and AI software that helps them get more customers.

pricing.model: Tiered monthly subscription; GoHighLevel requires resale at $97+/month

price_points.label: minimum resale price under GoHighLevel rules
typical reseller price range per Koerner
stated platform cost for the reseller (as spoken)

pricing.notes: Koerner says most charge $200-$500/month, some over $1,000. The $4.97 platform cost figure is as spoken; later he uses $497 in his examples, so the transcript is inconsistent.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook/Instagram vertical video ads, 15-45 seconds, many tested; copy winning ads found in the Meta Ads Library.

ideas.delivery: Software is white-labelled from GoHighLevel using templates; larger operators add remote overseas VAs and AI agents for service work.
unit_economics_claims: Margins about 98% with no staff, 50%+ with employees
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated precisely; platform cost quoted as $4.97/month (spoken) and a GoHighLevel trial of 14-30 days via affiliate link.

acquisition.how: Meta/Google ad creative can be generated by LLMs and run with routine human checks; owner reviews performance.

onboarding.how: Sub-account creation and template snapshots are software-driven; humans verify business details and number registration.

delivery.how: Software is mostly templated; service add-ons can be agent-run with occasional approval.

billing.how: Recurring subscription billing is handled by the platform.

support.how: AI agents can handle tier-1 support; Koerner's examples use VAs at $4-12/hour.

uk_applicability.notes: GoHighLevel is available in the UK. Pricing in GBP, UK phone number regulatory bundles and PECR/GDPR consent rules apply. Ads to UK local firms are fine; cold SMS/DM to sole traders is not.

risks: Customer counts are public tier thresholds, not exact; revenue is estimated
Dependence on GoHighLevel pricing and policy
Churn among small local businesses is not discussed

ideas.name: Missed call text back service for roofers
ideas.one_liner: Sell an automatic SMS reply with a booking link to roofers who miss calls while on the roof, as a wedge product for more services.
ideas.business_model: Monthly recurring fee, with upsells to ads, websites, etc.
ideas.customer: Roofing companies using personal cell numbers
ideas.problem: Missed calls while on a roof or with a customer lose jobs worth around $30,000.
ideas.offer: Instant text on any missed call with a link to book a roof inspection.

price_points.label: 'a hundred or multiple hundreds' per month
cost of phone number to the agency

pricing.notes: Koerner also mentions $1,000/month for his own marketing services.

acquisition_channels.details: Demo to a roofer from your phone in about 90 seconds; Koerner does not specify how to find roofers. His other examples rely on Meta ads.

ideas.delivery: Create a GoHighLevel sub-account, buy a local-area-code number, forward the roofer's calls to it with a 20-second ring timeout and voicemail off, then use the 'Missed Call Text Back' workflow template with a calendar booking link.
ideas.startup_cost: $1.15 per number plus GoHighLevel agency subscription

acquisition.how: Needs outreach to roofers; PECR limits cold SMS/DM to sole traders, so ads or cold email to limited companies are needed.

onboarding.how: Template-driven setup but needs number verification and call forwarding by the owner.

delivery.how: Workflow runs unattended once set up.

uk_applicability.notes: UK roofers have the same missed-call problem. Requires UK numbers and registration, PECR/GDPR compliance for texts, and call forwarding with mobile networks.

risks: If voicemail is on, the call counts as answered and the text never fires

tactics.name: Estimate competitor revenue from the awards page
steps: Find the competitor's public pricing page
Look up their SaaSpreneur tier (gold 100+, platinum 500+, diamond 1,000+)
Multiply price by the tier's minimum customer count
Weight tiers (most on cheapest, 10-15% middle, 5-10% top) for an average price

tactics.name: Reverse-engineer a competitor with five free tools
steps: Pricing page x customer count
Wayback Machine to see how the niche narrowed over 5 years
Meta Ads Library to find long-running (profitable) ads
BuiltWith for the tech stack
LinkedIn for employee count and roles to estimate payroll

tactics.name: Copy long-running and high-impression Meta ads
steps: Search the brand in the Meta Ads Library
Find ads active the longest, or sort by impressions
Spot recent ads with high impressions, as these are being scaled
Screenshot and ask an LLM to produce 35 similar ads for your business
Check the UK Ads Library for targeting information

quote.text: you go to the UK version of the Meta Ads Library, and they are required, if you're running ads in the UK, the Facebook is required to show the world who you are targeting with those ads.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Pick adjacent niches with an LLM
steps: Prompt an LLM with a proven niche and ask for 10 similar industries from first principles
Pick one and run it for a couple of months
Switch if it fails

quote.text: Dumpster rentals, porta potty rentals, skid steer and mini excavator rentals.

tactics.name: Missed call text back setup in GoHighLevel
steps: Create a sub-account for the customer (e.g. home services roofing)
Buy a local-area-code number for SMS and calls
Verify identity for regulatory compliance
Forward the owner's cell to the new number with a 20-second ring timeout, voicemail off
Use the Missed Call Text Back workflow template with a short delay
Create a roof inspection calendar and put its link in the SMS

tactics.name: Use a wedge product
steps: Lead with a quick-win product (missed call text back) demo-able in 90 seconds
Earn trust
Upsell ads, websites and other services

quote.text: I call this a wedge product. You wedge yourself into this business, earn their trust
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Find hidden pricing via Google
steps: If a site says 'book a strategy call', Google '<brand> agency pricing' to estimate retainer levels

warnings.warning: Don't rely on only 1-3 ads; most profitable advertisers test far more.

lessons.lesson: Public signals (customer tiers, pricing, ad longevity, headcount) let you estimate competitors' economics before building anything.
Serving boring local service niches with a 'make you more money' offer yields durable demand and easy sales.
Start broad, then narrow into the niche that says yes; the Wayback Machine shows a competitor's learning curve for free.

quote.text: Started generic, found the niche, they kept saying yes, and then narrowed down.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Ads that stay live for months are likely profitable; copy those rather than new ones.
Use a small wedge product to open a relationship, then upsell.
Lower-ticket software (CRM) scales to more customers than high-touch done-for-you services.
A high-ticket vertical (dental implants) allows large retainers because one new patient pays for the service.
Margins in software resale are high, but at scale you need overseas VAs and AI; payroll became about 25% of overhead in the Event Hawk guess.
Copy proven competitors rather than fear saturation: they take the arrows.

evidence_quality.rationale: All figures are the host's napkin-math estimates from public tier thresholds and guessed averages, not verified operator data. The roofing demo is first-hand and practical, but there is no real customer data and a price/cost inconsistency ($4.97 vs $497).
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris Koerner is a GoHighLevel affiliate and repeatedly asks viewers to use his link; he also sells marketing services and runs other GoHighLevel businesses.
